transcription.text: All that sort of stuff. Your first job at Anpex, what was, you were talking about VHS,
Anpex invented the VHS? Anpex at the Special Products Division, before I got there,
they had invented, they had developed the VHS recorder. And this was designed, it was done
for the government and it was for surveillance and they were, apparently they were flying plywood
drones over the Soviet Union to video, you know, sensitive military sites. So, they needed a
recorder. Who did they go to? Anpex had invented the video recorder. And so, you know, the cartridge
that you push the door down and then when it's done, it pops up, pops out. Well, for those
recorders, it popped all the way out to a parachute, was dropped from the drone, which
then went on to run out of fuel over the ocean and was snagged by an airplane. And
that all makes sense, doesn't it? It didn't really make sense to me when I saw it pop up. What is it?
And then Anpex had no idea what to do with it once the contract was done.
And I've heard this from some Anpex former executives, they really didn't know.
So, they gave it away to Japan Victor Corporation, JVC.
And it became the JVC.
You just gave it to them, there was no monetary?
Apparently not, not to hear of it. Or there might have been some trivial little
one-time payment or something. But they really blew that one. On the other hand,
JVC was a different kind of company than Anpex was. It's an interesting lesson.
Now, from my job there, I was designing analog electronics for high-speed tape duplicators
for the first two years. That's where I learned
how engineering is done, how things are documented and so forth.
